draft.title: Building and propaganda
card: Propaganda is the spread of ideas to shape what people think. Augustus used it to present his rule as the start of a new, peaceful age after years of civil war.
Monuments
The Ara Pacis, the Altar of Augustan Peace, honoured the peace he claimed to have brought. The Forum of Augustus displayed statues of Rome's great leaders, linking him to Rome's glory and its gods.
Coins
Coins carried his image and slogans, and passed through many hands across the empire. They spread his message to people who would never visit Rome.
Poets
Writers such as Virgil, in the Aeneid, linked Rome's past to Augustus's age. Poets who enjoyed the support of his circle often praised the peace and the new age.
draft.remember: Augustus used buildings, coins and poetry to present his rule as a peaceful golden age.

a.q: Why were coins a useful tool of propaganda for Augustus?
opts: They carried his image and slogans far across the empire
They made citizens swear loyalty each time they used them
They were made only for the Senate to read in Rome
They recorded the exact cost of each monument he built
a.why: Coins circulated widely, so his image and slogans reached people far from Rome. The claim that coins were meant only for the Senate is wrong, because their value as propaganda came from their wide spread.
a.clue: Think about how far coins travel and who handles them.

b.q: A historian reads Virgil's Aeneid and finds it praises Augustus's age. Why should she be careful about using it as evidence of what most Romans thought?
opts: Virgil was in Augustus's circle, so he may promote his image
Virgil wrote long after Augustus died, so it is unreliable
Virgil wrote it as a private diary, so it shows one view
Virgil was a foreign enemy of Rome, so it must be false
b.why: Virgil wrote within the circle of Augustus's supporters, so his praise may serve the regime's message. It is wrong to say it was written long after Augustus died, because Virgil wrote during his rule.
b.clue: Ask who supported the poet and what message that might favour.

a.best: They carried his image and slogans far across the empire

b.best: Virgil was in Augustus's circle, so he may promote his image

problems.detail: The card says poets who enjoyed the support of Augustus's circle praised the new age, but it never says that Virgil himself was one of them (through Maecenas's patronage). Question b depends on that fact, so students have to infer it. Adding a few words such as 'Virgil, supported by Augustus's friend Maecenas' would close the gap.
